==English==
[[Image:Bathroom in the Beamish Museum 01.JPG|thumb|right|200px|A bathroom with a primitive toilet in the UK's [[w:Beamish Museum|Beamish Museum]].]]
[[File:US Restroom.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A public bathroom ({{m|en|restroom}}) in the United States.]]

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|bath room|bath-room}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|id=lavatory|:af|bath<id:tub>|room<id:space>|tree=1}}
From {{compound|en|bath|room}}. Compare {{cog|nl|badkamer||bathroom}}, {{cog|de|Badezimmer||bathroom}}, {{cog|sv|badrum||bathroom}}, {{cog|fo|baðrúm|t=bathroom}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈbɑːθɹʊm/|/ˈbɑːθɹuːm/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|En-uk-bathroom.ogg|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈbæθˌɹum/|/ˈbæθɹʊm/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-bathroom.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈbæθɹʊm/|/ˈbæθɹuːm/|a=UK,US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʊm|uːm|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[room]] [[contain]]ing a [[shower]] or [[bathtub]], and {{q|typically but not necessarily}} a [[toilet]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:bathroom}}
#: {{hypo|en|Thesaurus:bathroom}}
#: {{hyper|en|room}}
# {{lb|en|chiefly|US|South Africa|Canada|Philippines|Australia|euphemism}} A [[lavatory]]: a [[room]] [[contain]]ing a [[toilet]] and {{label|en|typically but not necessarily}} a [[bathtub]].
#: {{ux|en|Most Americans don't know 'WC' and many Brits mock ''''bathroom'''' but almost everyone understands 'toilet' or 'lavatory'.}}

====Usage notes====
* From the beginning of the 20th century, ''bathroom'' has been the generic word for a room with toilet facilities in American English,<ref>
{{R:GNV|water closet, bathroom, restroom, WC, lavatory, washroom, (mens room + men ' s room), (ladies room + women ' s room + ladies ' room)|corpus=17|startyear=1860}}</ref> whereas Britons have continued to say {{m|en|lavatory}} relatively more frequently, and often {{m|en|loo}} or {{m|en|WC}} for a room with a toilet but no bath. In some contexts, ''bathroom'' refers more particularly to the toilet facilities of a private residence, distinguished from public buildings' {{m|en|restroom}}''s'' (US), {{m|en|washroom}}''s'' (Canada), {{m|en|men's room}}''s'', {{m|en|ladies' room}}''s'', etc.
